title: Theta Telecom - KMS/BYOK & Key Lifecycle Onboarding Review
summary: High-level security review covering Redwood's support for customer-managed keys (BYOK), HSM attestations, key lifecycle (rotation, revocation, versioning), envelope encryption patterns, audit logging and SIEM integration, and regional key controls for data residency. Customer wants clear onboarding checklist and test plan for pilot.
topics: Per-region keys and data residency controls
action_items: Jonah Li (Redwood SE): Share BYOK import runbook + sample import token flow (due 2025-10-07)
Maya Patel (Redwood AE): Send pilot pricing + dedicated vs hosted per-tenant KMS options (due 2025-10-06)
Priya Sharma (Theta): Provide list of required compliance artifacts (SOC2/ISO) and expected retention windows (due 2025-10-09)
Samir Varma (Theta): Provision test VPC and temp AWS account for onboarding windows (due 2025-10-10)
next_steps: Redwood to deliver BYOK import guide and sample scripts
Schedule 90-min deep-dive lab for key import and rotation with Theta platform team
Theta to confirm regulatory regions needing key separation and data residency
Exchange CSV of SAML groups to map RBAC roles for key access
header:
Date: 2025-10-02 15:00 UTC
Duration: 53 minutes
Location: Zoom
Recording: https://fireflies.ai/recording/ff-20251002-theta-tel
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE); Jonah Li (Redwood SE); Priya Sharma (Theta Head of Security); Marco Reyes (Theta Cloud Architect); Elena Novak (Theta Legal); Samir Varma (Theta Platform)
Notes: Security review requested by Theta security org to validate encryption at rest/in transit and BYOK onboarding for pilot
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone thanks for joining, we got the whole team on. Quick intro, I'm Maya AE at Redwood, Jonah is our solutions engineer, and we saw the doc priya sent over.
[00:28] Priya Sharma: Thanks Maya, yeah want to make sure the key management piece is rock solid. We have strict residency and we need to use our own key material, preferably HSM-backed.
[00:45] Jonah Li: Totally, so high level Redwood supports envelope encryption where customer CMKs live in cloud KMS or HSM and we wrap the data key, we also have a private deployment option for per-tenant HSM.
[01:10] Marco Reyes: When you say wrap the data key, are you doing local key material on the instance or is it all via remote KMS callouts? We want minimal egress of raw key material.
[01:30] Jonah Li: Right, we never export plaintext data keys from service nodes. Pattern is: Redwood runtime requests a short-lived data key, KMS returns encrypted data key (EK) + plaintext? actually the plaintext data key is only present in memory in the runtime process then immediately used to encrypt and then zeroed. For BYOK imports we support two flows: cloud-KMS-import (AWS/GCP/Azure) and an HSM-attested offline import for private deployments.
[02:05] Priya Sharma: Can you repeat the offline import? Our legal wants to see attestation that the key was generated in an HSM level and hasn't been exfiltrated.
[02:20] Jonah Li: Sure. For on-prem/private we support direct HSM import via KMIP or vendor-specific import token. There's an attestation step where Redwood's ops will provide an HSM attestation report (FIPS 140-2/3 certificate and import audit) and we can provide a signed proof-of-origin for the key import. For hosted we lean on the cloud KMS provider's import token flow which includes key origin metadata.
[02:50] Elena Novak: Do you provide a certificate of destruction or any chain-of-custody evidence when keys are rotated or deleted? Our policy requires proof that old material was retired.
[03:05] Jonah Li: We can provide audit logs for key lifecycle events: import, rotate, disable, schedule deletion. They contain timestamps, actor principal, IP and an import id. For private customers we can add extra attestation steps. The certificate-of-destruction can be generated as part of the deletion workflow, note there's some manual step for HSM-based offline imports because of vendor constraints.
[03:35] Marco Reyes: How about key rotation mechanics — is it automatic or do we manage versions? We need ability to do instant revocation in case of compromise.
[03:50] Jonah Li: Redwood supports automated rotation policies and manual rotation. The runtime keeps versioning of keys; we do envelope encryption so you rotate the CMK and produce new wrapped data keys. You can opt for immediate revocation which invalidates new envelope decrypts after a cutoff and we keep ability to rewrap historical objects if you request a re-encrypt job. There is a tradeoff with cost and throughput during rewraps.
[04:25] Priya Sharma: Do audit logs include enough detail for our SIEM ingestion? We forward to Splunk/Elastic?
[04:35] Maya Patel: Yes we have an audit stream that can be exported via syslog, Kinesis or direct HTTPS to your SIEM. Events include key ID, key version, action, principal, region, request id. Retention configurable based on your plan.
[04:55] Samir Varma: Data residency — we need the keys to be resident in EU regions for EU customer data and for APAC in Singapore. Can Redwood restrict keys to region and prevent cross-region recovery?
[05:12] Jonah Li: You can create per-region CMKs. For hosted we allow you to pin CMKs to a region and restrict the runtime to that region, and we enforce access policies so keys can't be used outside region. For cross-region replication we require explicit allow list in configuration and logging.
[05:40] Marco Reyes: What KMS providers do you support? Do you support raw HSM private key imports?
[05:50] Jonah Li: We support AWS KMS (including import tokens), GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault in common flows. Raw private key import is sensitive: for cloud KMS we use import token patterns that wrap key material under provider rules, not raw export. For on-prem/private we can accept keys generated on your HSM via KMIP or vendor import, with attestation. We do not accept plaintext keys via email :)
[06:18] Priya Sharma: SLA around key access? Latency and availability targets?
[06:25] Maya Patel: For Redwood Dedicated we have SLOs for key-based encrypt/decrypt latency; for Hosted our SLA references KMS roundtrip so practical latency depends on provider. We'll share our SLO doc.
[06:40] Elena Novak: Are the KMS audit logs part of the SOC2 package? Where do we find them?
[06:48] Maya Patel: Yes audit logs and our control mappings are in the SOC2 artifact package. We can share a redacted SOC2 report and our ISO scope.
[07:05] Priya Sharma: Regarding key rotation and rewrap, if we rotate CMK frequently does that cause token invalidation for in-flight sessions (e.g., long-running model inference streams)?
[07:22] Jonah Li: Good question — typical flow: pre-authorized sessions keep a short-lived data key or session token; rotation of CMK doesn't instantly break sessions that have the plain key in memory until they expire, but new requests will encrypt with the new wrapped key. We recommend short session TTLs for sensitive workloads.
[07:55] Marco Reyes: We need to enforce RBAC on key usage — who gets decrypt privileges? Integration with SAML groups?
[08:05] Maya Patel: Redwood maps identity to RBAC roles. We integrate with SAML/SSO (okta, azure ad) and can map groups to roles like key-reader, key-admin. For customer-managed keys we can also require manual approval for key import by a security principal.
[08:32] Priya Sharma: We need separation of duties; key admins should not be the same as ops engineers who can deploy models. Can you enforce multi-person approval for destructive key ops?
[08:44] Jonah Li: Yes we support approval workflows for deletion or export; in private deployments you can require a second approver (MFA + attestation) before sensitive operations.
[09:05] Priya Sharma: On tamper evidence — how do you show someone tampered with the HSM or import flow?
[09:12] Jonah Li: HSM attestation includes hardware serial, firmware version, and a signed quote from the HSM. Combined with our import logs you can detect mismatches. For hosted providers we rely on provider attestation mechanisms.
[09:35] Marco Reyes: Is the key usage logged by Redwood service, the cloud KMS, or both? We want independent logs.
[09:44] Jonah Li: Both. Cloud KMS has its own logs and Redwood emits service-level logs. We correlate them with request ids so you can verify independent records. You can retain both for your compliance window.
[10:05] Elena Novak: Backups — if we do backups of data, are they encrypted with the same key? How do you prevent key leakage in backups?
[10:16] Jonah Li: Backup object store is encrypted with envelope keys; backups carry wrapped keys. Key-policy can restrict restore to certain principals and we can hold backups in region-specific buckets. For high-regulation customers we recommend private deployment with KMS in your VPC and no external backup copy without explicit approval.
[10:48] Priya Sharma: Regarding HSM FIPS level, do you support FIPS 140-3 and can you provide certs?
[10:56] Maya Patel: We can provide FIPS certificates for the HSMs we integrate with and vendor attestation. We'll attach certs to the SOC2/ISO artifact set for the pilot.
[11:08] Marco Reyes: For key rotation policy, what's the recommended cadence? We have thousands of keys across tenants.
[11:16] Jonah Li: It depends on sensitivity; common is quarterly for CMKs, but many teams rotate data keys per object or per session. Envelope patterns keep CMKs long-lived but small risk surface. We'll provide a recommended policy doc.
[11:37] Priya Sharma: Can we do key splitting/escrow? We want multi-party control over master keys.
[11:45] Jonah Li: We support split-key escrow for private deployments using threshold schemes, but it's not part of standard hosted flow. This would be an add-on; we can prototype a 3-of-5 split using HSM-backed key shares.
[12:05] Samir Varma: Practical question — how do we test rotation in pilot? We want reproducible steps to validate decryption of historical data after rotation.
[12:16] Jonah Li: We'll run a lab: import CMK, encrypt sample objects, rotate CMK and run rewrap job, verify object access, check audit logs and SIEM ingestion. We'll provide scripts.
[12:35] Priya Sharma: What about export restrictions? Our regulation says keys can never leave EEA in plaintext. How do you enforce that?
[12:46] Jonah Li: For hosted we enforce region-bound CMKs and block API calls that would export plaintext or import from outside allowed geography. For private, since you control the HSM, the keys never leave your infrastructure.
[13:05] Marco Reyes: Are there performance impacts when using BYOK vs Redwood-managed keys?
[13:12] Jonah Li: Slight overhead for extra KMS roundtrip if using remote KMS, but with caching of wrapped data keys and continuous batching we minimize latency. Dedicated plans can co-locate KMS for lower RTT.
[13:35] Priya Sharma: Can we get a demo of the import flow? Preferably a recorded screen or runbook.
[13:42] Maya Patel: Yes Jonah will share the runbook and setup a hands-on lab.
[13:50] Marco Reyes: Any gotchas with algorithm support? We require AES-256-GCM and RSA-PSS for signatures.
[13:59] Jonah Li: We support AES-256-GCM for symmetric envelopes; for asymmetric signatures we support RSA-PSS and ECDSA depending on provider. We'll list exact algorithms per provider in the runbook.
[14:20] Elena Novak: On contractual side, can you add a clause about key ownership and deletion responsibilities?
[14:28] Maya Patel: Yes we can propose language stating customer retains ownership of key material and Redwood will follow deletion requests subject to change-control in the contract. We'll have legal follow-up.
[14:50] Priya Sharma: One more: are there any limitations on the number of keys or rate limits on KMS ops per second we should plan for?
[14:59] Jonah Li: Cloud KMS has rate limits per account. Redwood will provide throughput guidance and we can advise sharding keys or applying caching strategies to stay below limits. Dedicated customers get higher quotas.
[15:20] Samir Varma: For ingress/egress controls, can we whitelabel the KMS endpoints or do you manage them?
[15:30] Jonah Li: For private deployments you control endpoints; for hosted we manage endpoints but you get VPC peering and private link. We can support private connectivity patterns.
[15:50] Priya Sharma: Are there any threat models where Redwood holds the ability to decrypt our data even with BYOK? We need to be certain of no backdoors.
[16:03] Jonah Li: With BYOK and correct policy, Redwood does not have the plaintext CMK. We rely on provider constraints and attestation. For absolute assurance we'd recommend private deployment where you manage HSM and keys yourself.
[16:30] Maya Patel: Ok wrapping up — recap of deliverables: Jonah runbook, lab session, Maya pricing and contract language, Theta to list residency regions and compliance artifacts.
[16:48] Priya Sharma: Sounds good. Also we will run a quick internal Q&A and come back with any blockers.
[17:00] Marco Reyes: One small item — can you include sample Splunk ingest mapping?
[17:08] Jonah Li: Yes will attach sample mapping and an example dashboard.
[17:20] Elena Novak: We'll expect SOC2 artifact share and draft legal language in the next week.
[17:30] Maya Patel: We'll aim to send everything by EOD Monday, given timezone differences.
[17:40] Priya Sharma: Great, thanks everyone.
[17:45] Maya Patel: Thanks, bye.

Notes: Transcript contains occasional mis-heard words (e.g., "K-V cash" for KV cache), and speaker overlap. Action items captured above.
questions: Can Redwood provide HSM attestation and FIPS certificates?
Does Redwood provide certificate-of-destruction / key deletion proof?
How are audit logs exported and what fields are included?
Can keys be pinned per-region and prevented from cross-region use?
